Daughter of Iliam, the wife of Uriah the Hitite. So David sent messengers to get her and she came to him, and he laid with her. She got pregnant. This story is problematic because a woman doesn't sleep with you just because you ask her to. Remember that Bashibba is married to Uria the Hittite. Yuria, the best soldier in David's army, is very popular among his men. If you're David, who are you afraid of? You're afraid of your Yuria. Yuria is the person you're most afraid of.

So now he has a problem because Bashiba is pregnant. David needs to fix this issue because if Uriah returns and discovers that his wife got pregnant while he was away, he'll know David slept with her. So David sent word to Joab to send Uria to him. When Uriah came to David, David asked how it's going and said, "You're a great warrior. Why don't you go see your wife?" But Uriah refused because he said, "Listen, your army is fighting for you. I cannot go sit with my wife and feel good about myself while your men are dying." 

Now David has a huge problem. So he writes to Joab and tells him to set Uria in the forefront of the hardest fighting and draw back from him so that he may be struck down and die. So David orders Uriah's assassination, and Joab tells David, "Your servant Uriah is dead." In the Bible, it says David fell in love with Basheba, but if you think about it, what probably happened was that David became jealous of Uria because he was so popular among the soldiers and feared that Yuria would betray him as Saul did. So he likely ordered the assassination to prevent this threat from arising.

The real story is that David felt threatened by Uria's popularity and killed him to marry his wife, showing he was better than Uria. The Bible frames the story differently, writing it as an apology for David to disguise his crimes, showing God favored David because David reflects and improves like God does. So David and God are the same in a way, making Yahweh favor David above everyone else.

When Bashibba hears that her husband is dead, she cries. Then David and Bashibba marry and have a son together. Nathan the prophet then goes to David with a story about two men: one rich and one poor. The rich man steals the poor man's sheep for his guest. When David gets angry, Nathan tells him he is that rich man. But in reality, David's crime was killing Uriah, not stealing Bashiba.
